title: U.S. House · Washington's 4th District
area: Central Washington, including the Tri-Cities (Kennewick, Pasco, Richland) and Yakima Valley.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Dan Newhouse (R) is listed by Ballotpedia among the district's "withdrawn or disqualified" 2026 primary candidates and did not appear on the August 4 primary ballot, leaving this an open-seat race. Amanda McKinney (R) led the top-two primary with 34.9% of the vote, followed by John Duresky (D) with 30.8%, out of eleven primary candidates including Jerrod Sessler and state Sen. Matt Boehnke.

candidates.name: Amanda McKinney
candidates.ballotNote: Led the August 4 top-two primary with 34.9% of the vote

summary.text: Amanda McKinney is a Republican and a member of the Yakima County Board of Commissioners, first elected in 2020, who is running for the open 4th District seat after Rep. Dan Newhouse announced he would not seek reelection. She describes herself as an America First Republican whose priorities include defending faith, family, agriculture, and rural Washington. She led the August 4 top-two primary with 34.9%.

background.text: Was first elected to the Yakima County Board of Commissioners in 2020 and currently serves on it.

As commissioner, has focused on water and agriculture, including support for the Yakima Basin Integrated Plan, a county water bank built through senior water rights acquisition, and floodplain restoration projects; the Yakima Herald also reports she opposed prolonged COVID-19 shutdowns and vaccine mandates and has supported law enforcement, emergency communications, and efforts to address fentanyl and violent crime.
In 2024 she appeared in a television ad supporting Rep. Dan Newhouse's reelection against Jerrod Sessler, a Trump-endorsed Republican challenger.

Announced her congressional campaign days after Newhouse said he would not seek reelection; the seat is open for the first time in about a decade. Her seat on the county commission (Position 1) drew other candidates' filings for 2026.

Describes herself as an America First Republican aligned with President Trump on border security, the Second Amendment, and eliminating DEI programs. Trump endorsed her campaign on January 6, 2026, as did House Speaker Mike Johnson.

record.text: Serves as a Yakima County Commissioner.

candidates.name: John Duresky
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the August 4 top-two primary with 30.8% of the vote

summary.text: John Duresky is a Democrat from West Richland and a retired Air Force Major who spent 37 years in government service, including civil service as a project control officer at the Hanford Site. He left federal employment under an early-retirement offer in 2025 and is running for office for the first time in decades, campaigning on affordability, rural health care, and government accountability.

background.text: Describes himself as a veteran and a former federal civil servant with experience navigating VA and federal employment systems.
Retired Air Force Major. His campaign website says he served three combat deployments, and describes 37 years of service overall.
Worked in civil service for several years as a project control officer at the Hanford nuclear cleanup site.
Took the Department of Government Efficiency's early-resignation offer in 2025, ending 37 years of government service; he first passed on the offer and later chose early retirement.
Lives in West Richland and had attended Benton County Democratic Party meetings before running. This is his first campaign for office in decades, according to the Yakima Herald.

Signed the Take BAC Congress pledge (term limits, a lobbying moratorium, a ban on congressional stock trading, overturning Citizens United, and Supreme Court ethics rules). Endorsed by the Yakima County Democrats.

priorities.text: Lists affordability and economic fairness as a top priority, citing rising grocery, housing, health-premium and tariff costs, and calls for restoring congressional authority over tariffs.

On healthcare, says he will work to keep rural hospitals open, restore ACA subsidies, and protect Medicare and Medicaid, while saying he believes the nation should eventually move toward universal healthcare.
On immigration, calls for secure borders paired with a pathway to legal status and citizenship, and says ICE "requires major structural reform" based on his experience as a former civil servant.

Campaign website says he supports removing the stepped-up basis and carried-interest tax loopholes, raising the federal minimum wage, and protecting federal employees from what he calls politically motivated mass firings.

positions.summary: Supports restoring ACA subsidies, protecting Medicare and Medicaid, and says the country should move toward universal healthcare over time.
Calls for closing the stepped-up basis and carried-interest tax loopholes, which he says the wealthiest Americans use against everyone else.
Campaign website says he will fight to raise the federal minimum wage.
Says he will fight to remove tariffs that he says hurt farmers and raise consumer prices.
Supports secure borders alongside a pathway to legal status and citizenship, and says ICE needs major structural reform.

researchNotes: McKinney has not completed a Candidate Connection survey and no campaign website statement was found on her Ballotpedia page, so her positions and priorities could not be documented; researchDepth is minimal. Whether Rep. Dan Newhouse withdrew voluntarily or was excluded from the ballot was not independently confirmed beyond Ballotpedia's 'withdrawn or disqualified' listing. Biographical details such as McKinney's birthplace, education, and pre-office career were not found in the sources reviewed (no campaign-site biography page could be loaded).
